g.text: Mechanistic Interpretability of Safety Neurons in Vision-Language Models
Integrated Framework: Research Objectives, Research Questions, Screening Pipeline, Synthesis Findings & Deliverables
Identify neurons, attention heads, residual channels, circuits, and safety subspaces.
Appraise probing vs ablation, activation patching, dynamic steering, and subspace projection.
Determine whether safety neurons and refusal pathways are shared across text and vision.
Assess visual grounding loss, benchmark variability, reporting gaps, and adaptive threat risks.
How are safety concepts distributed across MLP neurons, heads, residual streams, and modalities?
Causal Role of Localized Units via Interventions
What can probing vs intervention (ablation, patching, steering, CARE) prove about causality?
Where do text and visual safety pathways intersect, and where does visual safety diverge?
Which reporting discrepancies, metric conflicts, and gaps impede real-world mechanistic safeguards?
• Traceable Bounded Scope: 30 Scholar search records captured on 18 Oct 2026.
• Complete Ledgers: Every record mapped in data/screening-records.csv.
• No Fabricated Numbers: 11 candidate studies without PDFs are formally acknowledged.
• Qualitative Synthesis: Disparate benchmarks evaluated without false pooling.
1. No Universal Safety Switch: Text refusal is compact (~88 neurons); visual safety is non-modular (50+ directions).
2. Decodability ≠ Causation: High probe AUROC does not prevent models from emitting harmful tokens.
3. Grounding vs Safety Trade-Off: Alignment overrides visual comprehension; requires joint utility auditing.
4. Dual-Use Circuit Threat: Circuit discovery enables SCIA attacks achieving 59.7% transferable ASR.
• G1: Test matched prompt triplets (text vs typographic OCR vs scene) under uniform intervention.
• G2: Mandate standardized reporting of injection layers, PCA cuts, and wall-clock latencies.
• G3: Concurrently audit Harmful Compliance Rate (HCR) and False Refusal Rate (FRR) on VQA/RefCOCO.
• G4 & G5: Evaluate low-resource language prompts and test against white-box adaptive attackers.
